candidate.answerReason: At x=-2, I contains only (-2,-4), II contains no point, and III contains every point on the vertical line x=-2.

methods.label: Test the exceptional input
methods.explanation:
A point belongs to an equation's graph when its coordinates make the equation defined and true. The denominator \(x+2\) in II suggests checking \(x=-2\).

For I, substituting \(x=-2\) gives \(y=-4\), so the graph contains \((-2,-4)\).

For II, the denominator is zero, so its graph contains no point with \(x=-2\).

For III, substitution gives \(0\cdot y=0\), which holds for every real \(y\). Its graph therefore contains the entire vertical line \(x=-2\).

Thus I and II differ at \((-2,-4)\), as do III and II. Also, \((-2,0)\) belongs to III but not I. Every pair of graphs is different, so the answer is \(\boxed{\mathrm{E}}\).
methods.levelReason: Substitution at one carefully chosen input distinguishes every pair of graphs without requiring factorization or advanced graphing.

needsNewNodes.description: Interpret the graph of an equation in x and y as all real ordered pairs for which both sides are defined and equal. Compare graphs by point membership, including excluded inputs, vertical lines, and equations that do not define functions.
